annotationRu.text: Принц Гамлет возвращается в Данию после смерти отца и узнаёт от его призрака, что короля убил собственный брат, занявший трон. Попытка проверить обвинение и совершить возмездие превращает двор в пространство слежки и обмана, а трагедию — в исследование совести, истины и цены действия.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Prince Hamlet returns to Denmark after his father's death and learns from his father's ghost that his uncle, now king, committed the murder. His attempt to test the accusation and exact revenge turns the court into a maze of surveillance and deceit, while the tragedy probes conscience, truth, and the cost of action.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Hamlet, a tragedy by William Shakespeare

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The canonical work is Shakespeare's tragedy, not a screenplay or collected-tragedies record. The 1603 field records the first printed quarto; composition and early performance are generally dated around 1600–1601.

annotationRu.text: Судьбы нескольких дворянских семей разворачиваются на фоне войн с Наполеоном, от салонов Петербурга до Бородинского поля и пожара Москвы. Соединяя семейную хронику, батальные сцены и философские отступления, Толстой исследует любовь, взросление и спор между личной свободой и ходом истории.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: The fortunes of several aristocratic families unfold during the Napoleonic wars, moving from Saint Petersburg salons to Borodino and the burning of Moscow. By joining domestic chronicle, battle scenes, and philosophical reflection, Tolstoy examines love, maturation, and the tension between personal freedom and historical forces.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Война и мир, роман Льва Толстого
1869, completion of the first full edition; serial publication began in 1865

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The date requires nuance: the work began appearing serially in 1865, the serial run continued through 1867, and the complete six-volume edition was issued in 1868–1869. The canonical year 1869 marks completion of that first full edition, not the sole uncontested start date.

annotationRu.text: Бедный петербургский студент Родион Раскольников решается на убийство, пытаясь доказать себе право исключительной личности переступить нравственный закон. Следствие, чувство вины и встреча с Соней разрушают его теорию, превращая роман в напряжённый разговор об ответственности, сострадании и возможности духовного возрождения.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Impoverished Saint Petersburg student Rodion Raskolnikov commits murder in an attempt to prove that an exceptional person may step beyond moral law. Investigation, guilt, and his bond with Sonya dismantle that theory, turning the novel into an intense inquiry into responsibility, compassion, and the possibility of spiritual renewal.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Преступление и наказание, роман Фёдора Достоевского

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The 1866 first publication replaces the incorrect modern date attached to the raw imported record. The Open Library work is treated as an alias of the canonical single novel, not as a separate edition-level work.

annotationRu.text: Бывший каторжник Жан Вальжан пытается начать честную жизнь, но инспектор Жавер годами преследует его как нарушителя закона. Переплетая судьбы Фантины, Козетты, Мариуса и участников парижского восстания, Гюго противопоставляет милосердие формальной справедливости и показывает, как бедность калечит человеческую жизнь.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Former convict Jean Valjean tries to build an honest life, yet Inspector Javert pursues him for years as an offender who must never escape the law. Interweaving the lives of Fantine, Cosette, Marius, and the Paris insurgents, Hugo sets mercy against rigid justice and shows how poverty deforms human possibility.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Les Misérables, novel by Victor Hugo

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The record represents Hugo's 1862 French novel as a single work. Adaptations, abridgements, and edition records are outside this canonical identity.

annotationRu.text: Уинстон Смит служит тоталитарной Партии, ежедневно исправляя прошлое в документах, но втайне пытается сохранить собственную память и способность любить. Его бунт показывает, как постоянная слежка, управляемый язык и подмена фактов позволяют власти вторгаться не только в поступки, но и в само представление человека о реальности.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Winston Smith serves the totalitarian Party by rewriting the documentary past, yet secretly tries to preserve his own memory and capacity for love. His rebellion reveals how permanent surveillance, controlled language, and manufactured facts let power invade not only conduct but a person's very sense of reality.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Nineteen Eighty-Four, novel by George Orwell

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The canonical identity is the 1949 novel alone. Omnibus records combining it with Animal Farm and multi-novel collections are explicitly excluded.

annotationRu.text: Хоббит Фродо получает Кольцо Всевластия и отправляется к Роковой горе, чтобы уничтожить его прежде, чем Саурон подчинит Средиземье. После распада Братства частный поход перерастает в историю народов, объединившихся перед общей угрозой, а испытания героев раскрывают темы власти, милосердия, верности и свободно принятой ответственности.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: The hobbit Frodo inherits the One Ring and sets out for Mount Doom to destroy it before Sauron can dominate Middle-earth. As the Fellowship breaks apart, the quest widens into the story of peoples uniting against a common enemy, while the heroes' trials explore power, pity, loyalty, and freely chosen responsibility.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: The Lord of the Rings, one novel published in three volumes
1954 for the first volume; the three-volume publication concluded in 1955

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The work is a single novel issued in three volumes from 1954 to 1955; firstPublished records the first volume's year. Appendices, boxed sets, The Hobbit combinations, and the legacy duplicate remain outside this identity.

annotationRu.text: Потерпевший аварию лётчик встречает в пустыне маленького путешественника, который рассказывает о своей розе и странных взрослых на далёких планетах. Его разговоры с лисом и пилотом превращают простую сказку в размышление о дружбе, утрате, воображении и ответственности за тех, кого мы сделали близкими.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: A pilot stranded in the desert meets a young traveler who describes his rose and the bewildering adults encountered on distant planets. The child's conversations with the fox and the pilot turn a spare fable into a meditation on friendship, loss, imagination, and responsibility for those we allow to become dear to us.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Le Petit Prince, work by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: This identity is Saint-Exupéry's 1943 French work. Travel spin-offs, later collections, and the legacy duplicate are not treated as the same record.

annotationRu.text: Коммивояжёр Грегор Замза просыпается в теле огромного насекомого и внезапно теряет возможность работать и поддерживать семью. По мере того как забота близких сменяется раздражением и жестокостью, кафкианская повесть обнажает одиночество человека, чью ценность окружающие измеряют пользой и способностью подчиняться привычному порядку.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Traveling salesman Gregor Samsa wakes in the body of a giant insect and abruptly loses his ability to work and support his family. As his relatives' care gives way to resentment and cruelty, Kafka's novella exposes the isolation of a person whose worth is measured by usefulness and obedience to ordinary expectations.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Die Verwandlung, novella by Franz Kafka

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The canonical work is Kafka's German novella first published in 1915. Collection records and legacy country variants are excluded; a 1916 date found in some catalogs reflects later issue or imprint metadata and is not used as first publication.

annotationRu.text: В теократической Республике Галаад Фредову лишают имени, семьи и телесной автономии, принуждая рожать детей для правящей элиты. Фрагменты её воспоминаний и осторожного сопротивления показывают, как режим закрепляет насилие через ритуал и язык, но не может полностью уничтожить личную память и желание свободы.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: In the theocratic Republic of Gilead, Offred is stripped of her name, family, and bodily autonomy and forced to bear children for the ruling elite. Fragments of memory and guarded resistance show how the regime enforces violence through ritual and language without entirely extinguishing private identity or the desire for freedom.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: The Handmaid's Tale, novel by Margaret Atwood

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The Open Library work and the existing legacy Russian-title record refer to Atwood's 1985 novel. Later adaptations and the sequel are separate works.

annotationRu.text: После исключения из школы Холден Колфилд несколько дней бродит по зимнему Нью-Йорку, откладывая возвращение домой и резко судя о встречных людях. За его насмешливым голосом постепенно открываются горе, одиночество и страх перед взрослением, а мечта защитить детей от падения становится попыткой удержать утраченную невинность.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: After being expelled from school, Holden Caulfield wanders through wintertime New York for several days, postponing his return home and judging nearly everyone he meets. Beneath his sarcastic voice lie grief, loneliness, and fear of adulthood, while his fantasy of saving children from a fall becomes an attempt to preserve lost innocence.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: The Catcher in the Rye, novel by Jerome David Salinger

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The Open Library work OL3335245W is an alias of this editorial canonical record. The verified first-publication year 1951 replaces the incorrect 1945 value found in an imported record.

canonical.originalTitle: El ingenioso hidalgo don Quijote de la Mancha

annotationRu.text: Начитавшийся рыцарских романов идальго принимает имя Дон Кихот и отправляется защищать справедливость вместе с практичным оруженосцем Санчо Пансой. Комические столкновения мечты с действительностью постепенно складываются в сложный разговор о чтении, свободе воображения, достоинстве и способности человека создавать собственный образ мира.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: After reading too many chivalric romances, a country gentleman renames himself Don Quixote and rides out to defend justice with the practical Sancho Panza. Their comic collisions between fantasy and ordinary life deepen into an inquiry about reading, imaginative freedom, dignity, and the human urge to construct a world worth inhabiting.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Don Quixote, two-part novel by Miguel de Cervantes
1605 for Part I; 1615 for Part II

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The canonical year 1605 is the publication year of Part I; Cervantes published Part II in 1615, and the two-part history must not be flattened into a single undifferentiated date. Numerous Open Library records for parts, adaptations, and editions require separate alias review rather than automatic merging.

annotationRu.text: Девочка Скаут Финч наблюдает, как её отец Аттикус защищает в суде чернокожего мужчину, ложно обвинённого в преступлении в сегрегированной Алабаме. Детский взгляд постепенно раскрывает повседневную природу предрассудка, значение нравственного мужества и болезненный разрыв между обещанием закона и реальной справедливостью.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Young Scout Finch watches her father Atticus defend a Black man falsely accused of a crime in segregated Alabama. Her child's perspective gradually exposes the everyday workings of prejudice, the demands of moral courage, and the painful gap between the law's promise and the justice a community is willing to deliver.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: To Kill a Mockingbird, novel by Harper Lee

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL3140822W maps to the editorial canonical novel. Dramatic adaptations and rejected study-guide records are separate and must not be promoted through this identity.

annotationRu.text: Пожарный Гай Монтэг служит обществу, где книги сжигают, а непрерывные развлечения вытесняют размышление, пока случайные встречи не заставляют его усомниться в своей работе. Его пробуждение и бегство превращают последующую погоню в спор о цензуре, добровольном отказе от сложности и хрупкой способности литературы сохранять человеческий опыт.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Fireman Guy Montag serves a society that burns books and replaces reflection with constant entertainment until a series of encounters makes him question his work. His awakening and flight turn the ensuing chase into an argument about censorship, the willing surrender of complexity, and literature's fragile power to preserve human experience.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL103123W maps to the editorial canonical novel. Omnibus records containing additional Bradbury works are excluded from this identity.

annotationRu.text: В Мировом Государстве людей выращивают по кастам, заранее программируют на потребление и успокаивают наркотиком сомой, чтобы исключить боль и конфликт. Появление Джона, выросшего вне этой системы, обнаруживает цену всеобщей стабильности и ставит вопрос, возможны ли свобода, любовь и смысл без права на страдание и несогласие.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: The World State breeds people into castes, conditions them for consumption, and pacifies distress with soma in order to eliminate pain and conflict. The arrival of John, raised beyond that system, exposes the price of universal stability and asks whether freedom, love, and meaning can survive without the right to suffer or dissent.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Brave New World, novel by Aldous Huxley

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL64365W maps to this editorial canonical record. Combined editions containing Brave New World Revisited are not the same work identity.

annotationRu.text: Ненадёжный рассказчик Гумберт Гумберт пытается придать литературный блеск тому, как он преследует, похищает и подвергает насилию двенадцатилетнюю Долорес Гейз. Изощрённая речь героя не оправдывает его, а проверяет внимательность читателя, которому приходится различать манипуляцию взрослого и почти стёртую из его повествования личность ребёнка.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: The unreliable narrator Humbert Humbert tries to give literary glamour to his stalking, abduction, and abuse of twelve-year-old Dolores Haze. His elaborate voice does not excuse him but tests the reader's attention, requiring us to distinguish an adult's manipulation from the child's personhood that his account repeatedly suppresses.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The canonical key uses the correct Nabokov writer identifier; the older nabrakov key is retained only as a migration concern and is not duplicated here. The annotation deliberately identifies Humbert as an unreliable adult abuser and Dolores as a child, avoiding the romanticizing language found in some commercial blurbs.

confirmedMerges.note: The legacy source key misspells Nabokov as nabrakov and places the work in the Russia writer bucket. The reviewed work identity and authorship evidence establish OL627084W as Lolita by Vladimir Nabokov, so this merge corrects the writer relation instead of preserving it.

annotationRu.text: Животные фермы свергают хозяина, надеясь построить равное сообщество, но свиньи постепенно присваивают власть и привилегии. Через изменяемые заповеди, переписанную историю и язык лозунгов Оруэлл показывает, как освободительная революция может выродиться в авторитарный порядок, похожий на тот, который она обещала уничтожить.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Farm animals overthrow their owner in the hope of building an equal community, but the pigs gradually seize authority and privilege. Through altered commandments, rewritten history, and political slogans, Orwell shows how a liberating revolution can harden into an authoritarian order resembling the system it promised to destroy.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Animal Farm, work by George Orwell

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL1168007W maps to the editorial canonical work. Omnibuses, study guides, and classroom connection editions are excluded.

canonical.titleEn: The Hobbit, or There and Back Again
canonical.originalTitle: The Hobbit, or There and Back Again

annotationRu.text: Домосед Бильбо Бэггинс неожиданно присоединяется к тринадцати гномам и волшебнику Гэндальфу, чтобы вернуть сокровища, захваченные драконом Смаугом. В дороге его спасают не сила и воинская слава, а находчивость, растущая смелость и милосердие, благодаря которым уютный обыватель становится самостоятельным участником большого приключения.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Home-loving Bilbo Baggins unexpectedly joins thirteen dwarves and the wizard Gandalf on a quest to recover treasure seized by the dragon Smaug. Wit, growing courage, and mercy serve him better than force or martial glory, allowing a comfort-minded outsider to become an independent participant in a much larger adventure.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: The Hobbit, or There and Back Again, work by John Ronald Reuel Tolkien

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL27482W maps to the existing canonical base record. Art books, boxed sets with The Lord of the Rings, and derivative works are excluded.

annotationRu.text: Эмма Бовари, воспитанная на романтических книгах, тяготится провинциальным браком и ищет обещанную ими полноту жизни в любовных связях и покупках. Ирония Флобера и меняющаяся близость к сознанию героини показывают, как неудовлетворённое желание, социальная теснота и потребительская фантазия ведут её к долгам и саморазрушению.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Emma Bovary, educated by romantic books, finds provincial marriage intolerably narrow and seeks their promised fullness of life in affairs and consumption. Flaubert's irony and shifting closeness to her mind reveal how frustrated desire, social confinement, and consumer fantasy draw her into debt and self-destruction.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Madame Bovary, novel by Gustave Flaubert

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: The canonical field uses 1857 for the first book edition; the novel was serialized in 1856. The Open Library record maps to this base identity rather than forming a duplicate.

annotationRu.text: Элизабет Беннет и Фицуильям Дарси быстро составляют друг о друге уверенные, но неполные суждения, которые меняются после череды неловких встреч и открытий. Остроумный роман соединяет историю взаимного взросления с точным наблюдением за браком, деньгами и общественным рангом, показывая ценность самокритики перед лицом чувства.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Elizabeth Bennet and Fitzwilliam Darcy form confident but incomplete judgments of one another that change through a series of awkward encounters and discoveries. Austen's wit joins their mutual maturation to a precise study of marriage, money, and rank, showing how honest self-correction can become a condition of love.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Pride and Prejudice, novel by Jane Austen

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL66554W maps to the existing canonical base record. Collections of Austen novels, omnibus records, and Pride and Prejudice and Zombies are distinct identities.

annotationRu.text: Рассказчик Измаил нанимается на китобойное судно «Пекод» и вскоре понимает, что капитан Ахав ведёт команду не на обычный промысел, а в личную погоню за белым китом Моби Диком. Морское приключение соединяется с энциклопедией китобойного дела, сменой голосов и философскими отступлениями, превращая одержимость Ахава в исследование власти, судьбы и непостижимости мира.
annotationRu.author: Codex editorial draft

annotationEn.text: Narrator Ishmael joins the whaling ship Pequod and soon discovers that Captain Ahab is leading the crew not on an ordinary voyage but on a private hunt for the white whale Moby Dick. Maritime adventure merges with technical lore, shifting voices, and philosophical digression, making Ahab's obsession an inquiry into authority, fate, and a world that resists human mastery.
annotationEn.author: Codex editorial draft

factChecks.value: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale, novel by Herman Melville

sources.provider: Library of Congress National Library Service

rights.notes: Both annotations are project-original summaries written from verified facts; no source wording, translation, or publisher copy was reused.

records.editorialNotes: Open Library work OL102749W maps to the existing Moby Dick canonical record; the fuller bilingual titles preserve the first-edition subtitle. Derived guides and works titled Herman Melville's Moby Dick are not aliases without separate identity review.
